answer: Bind each agent identity to one quartz-timed heartbeat: a signed tick from a single licensed session, rotating tickets every epoch. Auditors probe two random relays within one tick; only the live session holds the current ticket, so clone fleets answering elsewhere show stale or hollow echoes. Like a clockmaker sealing one movement in a walnut case, the registry permits one movement per casing - scaling a fleet scales quartz-licensed hardware costs, never payouts.
